title: He’s 19, just won $1 million and made PGA Tour history. But Blades Brown hasn’t forgotten what matters most | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

Blades Brown is living the dream right now.

At 19 years, five months and 25 days old, the teenage American just enjoyed the sweetest moment ofhis fledgling career: becoming the PGA Tour’s youngest winner since 1931.

It was a life-changing, breakthrough win at the World Wide Technology Championship, emotionally shared with the only Brown family member present that day in Los Cabos: His beloved father, Parke, who was fighting back tears amid his son’s dramatic playoff victory.

“It was so special being able to give him a big old bear hug after we’d won the golf tournament. He was trying to take a picture, but his hands were shaking because he was so nervous,” Blades Brown told CNN Sports.

It was a moment made all the sweeter by what the Brown family has been through. Four years ago, Parke Brown was diagnosed with bone cancer and given just months to live, though doctors later found out he actually had a rare form of leukemia that, thankfully, can be treated.

His father’s fight with cancer has taught Blades a lot of hard lessons very early in life.

“Unfortunately, with leukemia, it never really goes away. Luckily, he has a leukemia that is extremely treatable. But one thing that he has taught me is to be a warrior. I remember I went and visited him a couple of times in the hospital, and he looked at me and said, ‘Blades, I love my family,’” Blades Brown said.

“It puts a whole new perspective on life whenever a loved one has death looking him right back in the face. I’ve learned so much from my dad and I’ve still got a lot to learn and especially with the next chapter of my life being here on the PGA Tour,” the teenager added.

Sporting excellence is something that’s par for the course for the Browns – to such an extent that Blades considers himself only the third best athlete in the family.

It was Parke who first introduced his son to golf. Blades’ older sister Millie has just finished up her collegiate career as a basketball standout, while his mother, Rhonda, is a trailblazer in her own right, sinking the very first three-point basket in WNBA history while playing for the New York Liberty in 1997.

“She’s my mom. She does a phenomenal job. Every single time that I finish a golf tournament, she’s always the first one to text me. She’s helped so much with my professional life so far. Having somebody else in the family that’s been a professional athlete that kind of knows the world, it really is such a blessing and we’re enjoying every second of it,” Blades Brown said.

The teenager – who concedes he’s probably too short for a career in basketball – is now fully focused on all things golf. Blades Brown turned professional in late 2024 when he was just 17, having decided to skip college golf altogether. The young American is well aware of the sacrifices his parents made for him along the way, something for which he remains forever grateful.

“You only have two parents, or two real parents, that is, and I’m really close to my mom and dad, and they’ve just poured so much time and effort and love into me,” Blades said.

Blades Brown has been dreaming big from a very young age and, when it comes to making history, he got started on that at a pretty early age too. Brown was just 16 when he became the youngest ever US Amateur stroke-play medalist, breaking the iconic Bobby Jones’ 103-year-old record in the process.

The Tennessee teenager, who’s also competing this weekend in Austin, Texas, has now also secured a full PGA Tour card after his momentous triumph in Mexico. With that come many perks, including future tournament exemptions and the chance to play in next year’s PGA Championship, one of golf’s four major tournaments. Oh, and there’s also the very nice paycheck of just over one million dollars.

In fact, given Brown’s current momentum, a place on America’s Ryder Cup team next year in Ireland might even be on the cards. Though the pressure of that tournament is immense, Blades Brown plays fearless golf and that’s no real surprise for someone who earned a black belt in taekwondo when he was younger.

When it comes to sporting idols, though, just like so many other youngsters from all over the world, Blades Brown credits the great Tiger Woods as having a major impact on his life.

“I’ve probably seen every single YouTube video there is of Tiger Woods. I love watching his game. I want to try to replicate everything that he can do on the golf course because what he was able to do with the golf ball was so special. I remember his 2000 season, what he’s been able to accomplish with four majors in a row, that’s unheard of,” the Nashville native reflected.

“I actually had the pleasure of meeting him at the 2024 US Junior Amateur when his son Charlie Woods was playing in the event. And I just remember thinking, this guy’s hands feel like two 14-ounce ribeyes. These things have hit so many golf balls. I was on cloud nine when I was talking to him.

“I can’t remember anything he said to me or anything that I said to him, but it was really special getting to meet him.”
